questions.question: Which part of CSS contains the style rules?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The property and value (like color: blue;) contain the actual style rules that change how elements look. The selector just tells CSS which elements to apply the rules to.

questions.question: How do you select ALL paragraphs in CSS?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: p { } selects all paragraph elements. Element selectors use the tag name without any symbols. The dot (.) is for classes and hash (#) is for IDs.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔

questions.question: Which symbol is used for class selectors?

correct.details: Class selectors start with a dot: .className. Classes are reusable and can be applied to multiple elements on the same page.

questions.question: What's the best way to add CSS to a website?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: External stylesheets are best because they keep HTML and CSS separate, making code cleaner, easier to maintain, and allowing the same styles to be used across multiple pages.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔

questions.question: Which selects an element with id="header"?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: ID selectors use the hash symbol: #header. IDs should be unique on a page and are used for elements that appear only once.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔

questions.question: Where do you put internal CSS?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Internal CSS goes inside <style> tags in the <head> section of your HTML document. This keeps all styling information together at the top of the page.
